items.headline: Figma rebuilt its AI-impact study with AI — and says the measurement problem is the real story
items.excerpt: Figma revisits the study it started in 2024 on how AI reshapes design and product development, and this time uses AI to run the research itself. The post digs into what design orgs can actually measure about AI's effect on their work.

items.headline: Figma's Workflow Lab: keeping canvas and code in sync when agents write the front end
items.excerpt: Coding agents are reshaping how developers build, but they're only as good as the context they're given. Figma walks through a concrete workflow for moving between design and code with agents without losing design intent.

items.headline: Builder.io: agentic apps stitch design, SEO, analytics and finance into one launch loop
items.excerpt: Builder.io shows how agentic apps connect SEO, analytics, finance and design so siloed team workflows become launch-ready campaigns and working prototypes much faster.

items.headline: Vercel's Workflow SDK makes durable agent workflows look like ordinary code
items.excerpt: Vercel details how it built the Workflow SDK: durable workflows that read like normal code, run on infrastructure teams already have, and aim to make steps effectively free. It lowers the bar for designers prototyping multi-step agent products.

items.headline: Meta's Muse Image lands on Vercel AI Gateway — one key for image generation in prototypes
items.excerpt: Meta's Muse Image model is now callable through Vercel AI Gateway with a single API key: no provider account, automatic fallbacks, spend tracking and traces on every request. It makes image generation trivial to drop into a design prototype.

items.headline: AI in UX design: what actually changes in the craft, and what stubbornly doesn't
items.excerpt: A practitioner breakdown of which parts of UX work AI genuinely compresses — research synthesis, variant generation, copy — and which parts (judgment, framing, taste) it leaves untouched.

items.headline: Why generative room design fails on longer prompts — and wins on tighter constraints
items.excerpt: The first failed room concept usually gets the wrong diagnosis: designers add more prompt detail when the real fix is constraint design. A practical argument for treating spatial AI output as a constraint problem, not a prompting problem.

items.headline: Tripo's Smart Mesh generates game-ready topology in seconds, not retopo hours
items.excerpt: Tripo co-founder and chief scientist Dr. Yanpei Cao explains Smart Mesh — usable topology generated in seconds — plus Gaussian splats, more artist control over generated assets, and the shift from single-asset generation to whole interactive worlds.

items.headline: Nvidia's leaked DLSS 5 AI filter rewrites game art — and players hate it
items.excerpt: A leaked DLSS 5 AI filter that restyles character models is drawing an 'unsettling' reaction, with Final Fantasy 7's Cloud among the mangled examples. A live test of what happens when generative filters override an art director's intent.

items.headline: On-prem open-weight models are becoming the stable option for generative media pipelines
items.excerpt: fxguide looks at studios adopting open-weight generative models on-premises, and how that changes workflow stability, security, cost predictability and delivery efficiency versus API-only creative AI.

items.headline: Siemens' CEO on what AI inside product development software really changes for designers
items.excerpt: Siemens Digital Industries Software CEO Tony Hemmelgarn on how the platform is evolving, where AI is being integrated into product development tools, and what that means for the people doing the designing.

items.headline: AIA puts an AI assistant inside architecture's contract-document workflow
items.excerpt: AIA Contract Documents launched an AI Assistant for the industry-standard contracts architects and designers work from daily, alongside naming a new CTO — a sign of AI moving into the paperwork layer of design practice.

items.headline: An indie dev turned his pixel-art game into an AI-made series — and insists it stayed human-led
items.excerpt: HaZ Dulull adapted his own pixel art game Astro Burn into an animated series using AI tooling, while keeping creative direction firmly human. A concrete look at where AI sits inside a small creative team's pipeline.

items.headline: The real agent risk isn't autonomy — it's the complexity between the agents
items.excerpt: VentureBeat argues that enterprise AI failure modes come from the seams between agents rather than any single autonomous agent, which reframes how teams should design handoffs and review points.

items.headline: Orchestration becomes the new CX design problem in the age of AI agents
items.excerpt: As agents take over more customer touchpoints, the hard design work moves from individual screens to orchestrating the whole experience across agents and channels.

items.headline: 'Shadow agents' are the new shadow IT — and product teams are shipping them
items.excerpt: Shadow agents can act inside company systems before IT even knows they exist, making visibility and verification urgent. Relevant to any design org quietly wiring agents into its own tooling.

items.headline: AI has a hospitality problem money can't fix
items.excerpt: An argument that AI products keep failing at the hospitality layer — the felt sense of being hosted, guided and cared for — and that no amount of model spend fixes what is fundamentally a design problem.

items.headline: What Blade Runner got wrong about AI (so far)
items.excerpt: A designer's reading of how sci-fi's AI imagery diverges from the actual interfaces we ended up building, and what that gap suggests about designing today's AI products.

items.headline: Google's 'Listening area' turns Android XR glasses into a spatial AI translation UI
items.excerpt: Google is reportedly testing a 'Listening area' mode for Live Translate on Android XR — a spatial interaction pattern that could become the headline feature of its upcoming smart glasses.

items.headline: Matt Wolfe builds a full internal business app for free — no engineers involved
items.excerpt: Matt Wolfe walks through building a free app that runs an entire business operation using current AI builders — a hands-on look at how far prompt-to-app tooling has come for non-engineers.

items.headline: Putting Claude's new browser to real work
items.excerpt: A practical walkthrough of Claude's new browser agent on real tasks, showing where a browsing agent actually holds up inside a working day — research, competitive audits, repetitive UI chores.
